parakeet: Chapter 15 and Mark chapter 7. Christians love to say that Jesus was all about love and inclusion, that he welcomed everybody with open arms. But when we actually read the Gospels, we see a different picture. A Canaanite woman, a desperate mother, approaches Jesus, begging him to heal her sick daughter. What response does Jesus give? It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs. Not lost souls, not unbelievers, dogs. He dehumanized her. This is the language of supremacy. Throughout history, when groups have wanted to justify oppression, they start by reducing people to animals. Races called black people subhuman to justify slavery. Noxies called Jewish people rats to justify genocide. Colonizers called indigenous people savages to justify their destruction. Jesus was speaking directly in this tradition, placing his own people above outsiders. And before Christians say, oh, but he healed her daughter in the end, let's be clear. Only after she accepted her place beneath him did he grant her requests. This is not kindness.
